name: Pure
summary: Windows 11-inspired: a centered taskbar with Start, search, apps, tray and clock, and nothing else on screen.
description: A streamlined desktop with a single bar: a full-width taskbar with the JERONIX Start menu, search, Task View and your apps centered, and Quick Settings, notifications and the clock on the right. GNOME's top bar and desktop icons are hidden. All standard GNOME keyboard shortcuts keep working.

settings.reason: Original JERONIX icons; anything JERONIX does not draw falls back to Yaru and Adwaita.
Neutral system sounds instead of Ubuntu's Yaru sound theme.
Older (GTK 3) applications use GNOME's neutral dark theme instead of Ubuntu's Yaru.
A neutral interface typeface instead of Ubuntu's own.
Documents use the same neutral typeface.
JERONIX's primary look is dark; the light variant stays fully supported.
Ubuntu shows the slate accent as Yaru sage, the JERONIX secondary color, instead of Ubuntu orange.
The overview is Pure's workspace switcher, so it stays one gesture away.
The clock is the main persistent text in the panel; the weekday makes it useful at a glance.
Minimal title bars. Minimize and maximize remain available from the keyboard and by double-click.
Super opens the overview; Pure depends on it for keyboard-first navigation.
Workspaces appear and disappear as needed, so there is nothing to configure.
Secondary monitors stay put while workspaces switch, the GNOME default.
Drag-to-edge and Super+Left/Right tiling.
JERONIX light wallpaper.
JERONIX dark wallpaper.
Fill the screen without distortion.
Graphite shows while the wallpaper loads.
Lock screen matches the desktop.
The JERONIX name sits beside its symbol.
Fewer persistent elements; the overview shows workspaces.
A quiet top bar: menu, clock and status only.
The JERONIX menu replaces Activities.
A floating dock centered at the bottom.
Always visible like a Windows 11 taskbar; maximized windows stop above it.
Compact Windows 11 proportions.
Running applications appear after favorites.
Window previews on hover.
A full-width Windows 11-style taskbar.
Start, search and apps centered, as in Windows 11.
Quick Settings and the clock with notifications live in the taskbar tray.
One bar: GNOME's top bar is hidden while the taskbar carries the tray.
Task View opens the windows and workspaces overview.

limitations: Ubuntu's dock and desktop icons are switched off through disabled-extensions, never uninstalled; restoring the snapshot switches them back on.
Panel item order and the overview's own layout are GNOME's.
